 acts in the adjoint representation
on the curvature. Quantization additionally requires gauge fixing or a gauge-invariant construction, constraints, and, in

Nothing in the current assignment recovers a unique MK-43 gauge group or proves that a particular upstream field realizes

For a matter field 
, the ordinary derivative is replaced by
Equation (52.8) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. It links representation data, connection, and curvature. This is

The commutator relation is representation dependent. It must not be generalized to every propagation or continuation operator
without specifying how the operator acts on sections.

52.10 Gauge fixing and physical modes
The physical configuration space is a quotient,
Equation (52.10) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. A gauge choice selects representatives, while observables

52.12 Transverse-traceless gauge
For radiative perturbations on a suitable background, the TT conditions are
Equation (52.12) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. The address @transverse_traceless_gauge is MEDIUM
and strongly connected in Library 4.1. The conventional conditions isolate radiative degrees of freedom only under appropriate
background, field-equation, and boundary assumptions.
TT projection is therefore not a universal replacement for gauge reduction. It applies to a specified perturbative sector and
must preserve the upstream provenance of the perturbation being projected.
52.13 Gauge consistency is a typed condition
The recovered addresses are substantial, but address density cannot merge internal gauge theory, linearized diffeomorphisms,
and gauge fixing:
Equation (52.13) is EVIDENCE_AND_TYPE_BOUNDARY. The first two are transformation groups or their infinitesimal actions;
the last is a condition on representatives. Gauge consistency requires that the action, field equations, constraints, observables,
and quantization respect the relevant symmetry.
The API handle @gauge_consistency has MEDIUM coverage and two registered dependencies. Its indexed equation units
remain source windows to audit, not permission to assert a completed universal consistency theorem.

Chapter 53 - Spinor and Fermionic Realization
53.1 Clifford structure
Fermionic fields require more than a scalar bundle. On a spacetime with metric 
, gamma matrices provide a representation
of the Clifford algebra,
Equation (53.1) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. It is not a recovered equation from this chapter's eight
assigned Library addresses. The relation ties spinor representation theory directly to geometry and fixes the principal algebraic
condition a spinor realization must satisfy.
A choice of gamma matrices is representation dependent; the Clifford relation is invariant. Confusing one matrix representation
with the underlying Clifford module would repeat the identity-versus-representation error guarded against throughout the
TOME.
53.2 Spinor bundle
Given an admissible spin structure, spinor fields are sections
Equation (53.2) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Here 
 is a spinor bundle and  is Clifford multiplication. The
existence of 
 imposes topological conditions; it is not guaranteed by the existence of an arbitrary complex vector bundle 
.
Therefore the handoff object 
 can host a fermionic realization only after a spin or related structure and its representation
inside 
 are established.
53.3 Spin connection
Using a local orthonormal frame, the covariant derivative on spinors takes the form
Equation (53.3) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. The spin connection lifts the geometric connection to the
spinor representation. Its curvature acts on spinors through the corresponding Clifford generators.
This is an explicit example of action through geometry: the background connection affects fermionic propagation through 
.
The API address @action_through_geometry is THIN and contains no recovered equation, so the formula is not attributed to it.
53.4 Dirac action
A conventional curved-spacetime Dirac action is
Equation (53.4) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Hermiticity and boundary conditions may require an explicitly
symmetrized derivative form. The action depends on the spin structure, gamma representation, mass, orientation, and volume
form.
No current source record proves that @interaction_term or @zer0_interaction is the mass or interaction part of Equation (53.4).

A complete MK-43 realization must identify the spinor variable, its bundle, the operator domain, boundary conditions, and the

53.6 Conserved current
For the global phase symmetry of the free Dirac action,
Equation (53.6) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS on solutions with the corresponding adjoint equation. The
current illustrates how an observable bilinear descends from spinor fields.
Conservation is not inferred from an operator name. It follows from the action, symmetry, equations of motion, and boundary
assumptions.
53.7 Chirality projectors
In an even-dimensional setting with a chirality operator 
,
Equation (53.7) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. It defines left- and right-chiral spinor components in this
representation. The framework's broader chirality QMO carries organizational meaning beyond ordinary handedness, so the
two notions must not be identified by shared terminology.
An exact translation would need a typed map from organizational chirality into the eigenstructure of 
, together with
covariance and interaction compatibility.
53.8 Mass and chirality coupling
A Dirac mass couples opposite chiralities,
Equation (53.8) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Chiral gauge theories can restrict which mass terms are
allowed before symmetry breaking. This makes representation and charge assignments inseparable from the interaction
structure.
No source evidence in this assignment fixes an MK-43 fermion mass-generation mechanism, chirality representation, or
symmetry-breaking sector.
53.9 Fermionic anticommutation relations
Quantized fermionic modes satisfy the canonical anticommutation relations
Equation (53.9) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Anticommutation enforces fermionic statistics and finite
occupation per mode. It is categorically different from the bosonic commutator algebra discussed in Chapter 50.
The algebra requires a mode space and inner product. A generic object called an annihilation operator does not become
fermionic until these relations and the relevant domain are established.

53.10 Fermionic Fock space
For one-particle space , the fermionic Fock space is
Equation (53.10) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. The antisymmetric exterior powers encode the Pauli
exclusion structure. The number operator counts excitations relative to the selected mode representation.
Fock space is a representation tool, not proof that fermions are fundamental points or that a unique particle interpretation exists
on every background.
53.11 The Genesis annihilation address
Library 4.1 declares @operator_14_4_genesis_annihilation_operator but provides only three coherent English units, no
equation units, and no registered dependencies. A conventional annihilation action is
Equation (53.11) is EXTERNAL_MATHEMATICS_AND_EVIDENCE_BOUNDARY. The phase sign depends on mode ordering.
The formula is not a recovered definition of the Genesis operator. The source must establish whether that address removes a
fermionic excitation, transforms an organizational state, acts in Genesis-language space, or performs another operation.
Shared use of the word annihilation is insufficient for identity.
53.12 Yukawa interaction
A standard scalar-fermion coupling is
Equation (53.12) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. More general chiral or multiplet couplings require
representation indices and invariant tensors. Coupling constants, dimensions, and renormalization depend on the theory.
The thin address @interaction_term and the medium address @zer0_interaction do not supply a clean recovered equation
selecting Equation (53.12). The latter has one indexed equation window and 27 dependencies, but the window is not treated as
a topic-defining formula without exact source isolation.
53.13 Observable operator algebra
Fermionic observables lie in an even subalgebra generated by bilinears such as
Equation (53.13) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS as a schematic inclusion. The API declares
@observable_operator_algebra, but its THIN coverage contains no equation or dependency record. A full algebra needs
topology, involution, representation, domain, and superselection data.
Odd field operators can change fermion parity, while observables are normally parity even. That distinction must be preserved
in any MK-43 operator registry.

The conventional fermionic pipeline can be summarized without asserting an MK-43 identity:

Chapter 54 - Yang-Mills and Non-Abelian Structure
54.1 Lie algebra data
A non-Abelian gauge theory begins with a Lie group 
, its Lie algebra , and generators satisfying
Equation (54.1) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. The structure constants encode the local algebra in a chosen
basis. The group, representation, normalization of generators, and coupling are independent inputs; none is fixed by this
chapter's three assigned API handles.
The noncommutativity of the generators is the source of gauge-field self-interaction. It distinguishes Yang-Mills structure from
an Abelian superposition of independent vector fields.
54.2 Connection transformation
For a Lie-algebra-valued connection 
, a local gauge transformation 
 acts as
Equation (54.2) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS for the displayed convention. The inhomogeneous term is
required for the covariant derivative to transform covariantly.
Gauge transformation is a change of local representative, not a physical propagation law. An API operator needs an explicitly
declared action on the bundle before it can be identified with Equation (54.2).
54.3 Non-Abelian curvature
The field strength is
Equation (54.3) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. The commutator term makes the field strength nonlinear in
the potential and produces three- and four-gauge-boson vertices when the action is expanded.
The connection and curvature entries of 
 provide an abstract home for this pair, but a source-level Yang-Mills realization still
requires the principal bundle, structure group, and representation map.
54.4 Covariance of curvature
Under Equation (54.2),
Equation (54.4) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. The curvature transforms homogeneously, so invariant traces
of products of 
 can define gauge-invariant action densities and observables.
This is the precise distinction between covariance and invariance. A matrix-valued field strength changes by conjugation, while
a properly normalized trace such as 
 is invariant.

54.6 Yang-Mills action
Using an invariant bilinear form on ,
Equation (54.6) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Gauge invariance depends on the invariance of the trace.
Boundary terms, topology, theta terms, matter couplings, and quantum corrections can enlarge the action.
No assigned handle supplies an exact recovered Yang-Mills action. The formula is the conventional target for testing whether
the handoff connection realizes a gauge field.
54.7 Yang-Mills equation
Variation gives
Equation (54.7) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS under the corresponding matter equations and conventions.
The covariant conservation law is the compatibility condition required by gauge symmetry.
Unlike the Abelian equation, the gauge field itself contributes to the nonlinear dynamics through 
 and 
.
54.8 Gauss constraint and physical states
In canonical form, the temporal gauge component acts as a constraint multiplier and physical states obey a Gauss-law
condition of the form
Equation (54.8) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS schematically. Quantization must retain the constraint algebra
and remove gauge redundancy without removing physical degrees of freedom.
The condition makes clear why a creation operator on an unconstrained mode space is not automatically a physical Yang-Mills
operator.
54.9 Wilson loops
A basic gauge-invariant nonlocal observable is the Wilson loop
Equation (54.9) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. The path-ordering symbol 
 is required because connection
values at different points need not commute. The representation 
 and closed curve 
 are part of the observable.
Wilson loops expose global and topological information not captured by a local field-strength value alone.

54.11 Creation operators and gauge modes
After gauge reduction and a mode choice, a perturbative gauge field can be expanded schematically as
Equation (54.11) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. The created excitation depends on gauge fixing,
polarization, constraints, vacuum, and perturbative regime.
Library 4.1 classifies @creation_operator as a CREATED operator with THIN coverage and three dependencies. That record

; an exact definition and algebra are still required.
54.12 Self-interaction structure
Expanding the curvature term in Equation (54.6) produces schematic orders
Equation (54.12) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. The quadratic term controls free propagation, while the
cubic and quartic terms encode non-Abelian self-interaction. Their explicit coefficients follow from the structure constants and
conventions.
This hierarchy is a perturbative organization, not a claim that the full quantum theory is weakly coupled.
54.13 Stress-energy and backreaction
Metric variation yields a gauge-field stress tensor of the form
Equation (54.13) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS for the standard action convention. It supplies the object that
can source geometric backreaction.
The API address @backreaction is MEDIUM with 45 English units, five indexed equation units, and 213 dependencies. Those
windows are not treated as a clean native Yang-Mills backreaction equation without source isolation.

55.1 Action as the dynamical organizer
For fields 
 on a spacetime region 
, a local action has the conventional form
Equation (55.1) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. An action is more than a list of allowed terms: it fixes the
variational problem, boundary data, equations of motion, and—when symmetries are present—the corresponding conservation
identities. The field content, dimensions, couplings, and admissible variations must therefore be stated before a native MK-43
action can be considered complete.
The ten Library 4.1 addresses assigned to this chapter organize operator-related evidence. They do not independently supply
a single recovered action functional.
55.2 Euler-Lagrange equations
Stationarity under compactly supported variations gives
Equation (55.2) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Its use requires differentiability of the action and controlled
boundary terms. Constraints, gauge freedom, higher derivatives, and nonlocal kernels change the precise variational analysis.
An API object called an operator becomes dynamical only after its domain, codomain, action on fields, and relation to 
 are
supplied. A registry address alone does not establish Equation (55.2) for its entries.

Equation (55.3) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS on shell. Global charges require appropriate hypersurfaces

more carefully than ordinary global charges.
Conservation in this chapter means a demonstrated consequence of a stated symmetry and action, not merely persistence
suggested by an operator's name.

Chapter 56 - Measurement and Readable Quantum Structure
56.1 Measurement as an operational map
A quantum measurement begins with a state space, an outcome space, and a rule connecting them. In its most general
standard form a measurement is a positive-operator-valued measure (POVM)
Equation (56.1) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Here 
 is a sigma-algebra of outcomes and 
 is an
operator space. Readability requires more than a state: it requires an outcome vocabulary and a calibrated map from physical
interactions to records.
The seven Library 4.1 addresses assigned to this chapter are all THIN. They organize recovery and expansion operations, but
no address supplies a recovered native measurement theory by itself.
56.2 Born probabilities
For a density operator , the probability of an outcome in 
 is
Equation (56.2) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Positivity ensures nonnegative probabilities and
normalization ensures unity for the complete outcome space. A native MK-43 account must identify the physical state,
observable interface, and meaning of the outcome labels before Equation (56.2) can be applied.
56.3 Projective measurement
A projective measurement is the special case
Equation (56.3) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Its orthogonal projectors resolve the identity, but not every
physical measurement is projective. Coarse graining, detector inefficiency, and indirect coupling naturally lead to general
POVMs.
The word “projection” in upstream framework material must not be identified with 
 unless its domain, codomain,
idempotence, and measurement role are explicitly recovered.
56.4 Instruments and state update
A quantum instrument associates each outcome with a completely positive map 
. The probability and conditional state are
Equation (56.4) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. It separates an observed probability from the post-
measurement state. A “recover” or “normalize” operation in a metadata architecture is not automatically a physical instrument.

Chapter 58 - Graviton Identity and Projection Mode
58.1 Identity boundary
The API architecture keeps three objects distinct:
Equation (58.1) is DETERMINISTIC_API_EVIDENCE. It expresses scoped mode and projection relations, not whole-object
identity. Helicon is the upstream organizational domain; gravitational Helicon mode is a gravity-relevant mode; graviton is its
downstream projected realization in the current candidate architecture.
Conventional particle language remains a representation vocabulary. It must not erase the operative coherent-mode and
projection-mode distinctions.
58.2 Downstream projection
The recovered dependency continues as
Equation (58.2) is DETERMINISTIC_API_EVIDENCE. A graviton is not identified directly with the full metric perturbation.
Continuity perturbation and Time-Shell projection are explicit intermediate stages.

VOLUME VII - GRAVITY
Chapter 61 - Weak-Field Metric and Curvature
61.1 From projected metric to curvature
The weak-field regime begins with a background metric and a small symmetric perturbation,
Equation (61.1) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. In the TOME sequence, the prior Time-Shell projection
chapter supplies the candidate perturbative output 
; this chapter asks what geometric structures follow once that output is
admitted as a metric perturbation. It does not identify the Time Shell, the projection operator, the perturbation, and curvature.
61.2 Perturbative order
Introduce a bookkeeping parameter :
Equation (61.2) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Linearized quantities are first variations at a fixed
background. A result valid at 
 is not silently promoted to a nonlinear curvature law.
61.3 Inverse-metric variation
The first inverse-metric variation is
Equation (61.3) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Raising an index with the background metric is part of the
perturbative convention and must not be confused with using the unknown full inverse metric.
61.4 Connection perturbation
For the Levi-Civita connection of the background,
Equation (61.4) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. It supplies the exact linear bridge from a metric perturbation
to a connection perturbation. The Library keeps @connection_and_curvature and @connection_to_formal_curvature_bundle
distinct because a conceptual pairing is not itself a typed bundle construction.
61.5 Linearized Riemann curvature
The corresponding first variation of the Riemann tensor is
Equation (61.5) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Curvature is therefore second order in derivatives of the
metric perturbation at linear order. It is not an additional independent field once the metric connection is fixed.

61.10 Bianchi identity
The curvature two-form obeys
Equation (61.10) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. This identity constrains any candidate curvature binding. A
proposed binding that violates it cannot represent the curvature of a compatible connection without additional structure.

61.15 Curvature singularity criterion
A coordinate divergence is not sufficient evidence of a curvature singularity. An invariant diagnostic is the Kretschmann scalar,
Equation (61.15) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Divergence of 
 can certify invariant curvature blow-up in a
given solution, while finiteness alone need not prove global regularity.

VOLUME VII - GRAVITY
Chapter 62 - Einstein Sector and Stress-Energy
62.1 The dynamical threshold
Curvature becomes a gravitational field equation only when geometry is related to a source sector:
Equation (62.1) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. The Einstein tensor, cosmological term, metric, and stress-
energy tensor occupy different mathematical roles. The equation does not identify geometry with matter; it constrains them
through a covariant relation.
62.2 Einstein-Hilbert action
For a metric theory with cosmological constant, the gravitational action is
Equation (62.2) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. @einstein_hilbert_action has MEDIUM coverage and a
dense dependency neighborhood, but a familiar title does not by itself establish the action as the complete native MK-43
dynamics.
62.3 Stress-energy from matter variation
Given a matter action 
, define
Equation (62.3) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS for the displayed sign convention. Stress-energy is therefore a
metric response of the matter action. A proposed MK-43 source must specify its fields, action or constitutive rule, and
variational dependence before it can be inserted as 
.
62.4 Metric variation
For the total action 
, stationary variation gives
after the required boundary treatment. Equation (62.4) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. This action-to-
equation implication is conditional on differentiability, admissible variations, and boundary conditions.
62.5 Conservation compatibility
The contracted Bianchi identity implies
Equation (62.5) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS when Equation (62.1) holds with constant 
 and 
. Any
additional source sector must be compatible with this covariant conservation law or explicitly modify the geometric side.

62.7 Riemann symmetries
For a Levi-Civita connection,
Equation (62.7) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. These algebraic identities are typing constraints on any

62.8 Linearized Einstein tensor
On a flat background, the first-order Einstein tensor is
Equation (62.8) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. @linearized_einstein_tensor has MEDIUM coverage with

62.9 Linearized gauge freedom
An infinitesimal coordinate change generated by 
 acts as
Equation (62.9) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Gauge-related perturbations describe the same linearized
geometry. A projection output must therefore be interpreted modulo the relevant gauge relation unless a gauge is fixed.
62.10 Trace reversal
Define the trace-reversed perturbation by

Equation (63.2) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Its derivation assumes a flat background, weak perturbations,

Equation (63.3) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. The null dispersion relation and transversality condition follow

Equation (63.4) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. TT gauge isolates the two radiative degrees of freedom in

Equation (63.5) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. The plus and cross tensors depend on a transverse basis.

radiative degrees of freedom in general relativity. Equation (64.2) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS as the

Chapter 76 - Coupling Operators and Relations
76.1 Operators have domains
A linear coupling operator is a map
Equation (76.1) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. The domain is part of the operator; a symbolic rule without
 may fail to define a map on relevant states.
76.2 Boundedness
An operator is bounded when
Equation (76.2) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Bounded operators extend continuously to the full Hilbert
space; many differential coupling operators do not.
76.3 Adjoint relation
The adjoint is defined by
Equation (76.3) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS on the appropriate domains. Adjointness depends on the
inner products and boundary conditions.

Chapter 109 - Consciousness as a Phase-Coherent Domain
109.1 Typed consciousness-hypothesis record
A scientific consciousness hypothesis must keep its carrier, state space, dynamics, observables, report criteria, and validation
domain separate,
Equation (109.1) is DETERMINISTIC_TYPE_NORMALIZATION. It is a chapter contract rather than a recovered definition of
consciousness. In particular, a mathematical order parameter cannot stand in for a report, behavior, or experience without an
explicit bridge.
109.2 Phase-field comparison
A phase-coherent-domain proposal may begin with a complex field,
Equation (109.2) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Its amplitude, phase, carrier, domain, and measurement
protocol must be supplied before it can represent any biological or cognitive phenomenon.
109.3 Global phase coherence
For a declared ensemble of phases, coherence may be summarized by
Equation (109.3) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. The scalar magnitude records phase concentration in the
ensemble; it is not an intrinsic measurement of consciousness.
109.4 Spatial correlation
A stationary field may be examined through a two-point correlation function,
Equation (109.4) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Correlation length and decay law are empirical properties of
a specified observable, not evidence of phenomenology on their own.
109.5 Coupled phase dynamics
A conventional comparison model for interacting phases is
Equation (109.5) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. It provides a synchronization scaffold, not the recovered
dynamics of the address @consciousness.

Chapter 110 - Perception, Memory, and Temporal Integration
110.1 Typed perception-memory record
A perception and memory model must distinguish latent state, sensory data, internal map, temporal store, decision criterion,
and report,
Equation (110.1) is DETERMINISTIC_TYPE_NORMALIZATION. It is a chapter contract, not the native definition of any
assigned handle. Each map needs a domain, codomain, scale, and observable interpretation.
110.2 Observation model
A standard perceptual comparison begins with latent state and noisy observation,
Equation (110.2) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. The function and noise distribution must be estimated; the
equation does not assert that perception is passive reconstruction.
110.3 Bayesian filtering
Sequential state estimation can be represented by
Equation (110.3) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. It is a comparison scaffold, not the recovered content of
@internal_experiential_map.

A temporal store may be modeled as a weighted history,
Equation (110.4) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. The kernel, horizon, retained variables, update law, and
biological carrier require independent evidence.
110.5 Temporal integration window
A normalized integration window satisfies
Equation (110.5) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. An integration interval is an operational parameter, not a
recovered universal duration of perception.

Chapter 111 - Agency, Autonomy, and Environmental Coupling
111.1 Typed agency record
An agency model must distinguish system state, action, environment, policy, constraints, objective, observables, and
validation,
Equation (111.1) is DETERMINISTIC_TYPE_NORMALIZATION. It is a chapter contract rather than a recovered definition of
agency or autonomy. Mathematical influence and ethical or personal agency occupy different explanatory levels.
111.2 Controlled dynamics
A standard system-environment comparison is
Equation (111.2) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Bidirectional coupling does not by itself establish control,
intention, autonomy, or cognition.
111.3 Policy representation
A stochastic policy can be represented by
Equation (111.3) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. A policy is a mathematical conditional distribution and need
not be conscious, reflective, or freely chosen.
111.4 Action influence
A generic information-theoretic influence statistic is
Equation (111.4) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Conditional dependence does not prove causation unless
interventions and confound controls are supplied, and it is not a complete agency measure.
111.5 Constraint feasibility
A constrained action set can be written
Equation (111.5) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Constraints may be physical, informational, environmental,
or imposed; their presence alone does not determine whether a system is autonomous.

Equation (111.13) is EVIDENCE_BOUNDARY. The three THIN addresses do not establish a common scale, units,

119.1 Typed audit record
A reproducible validation claim requires a typed record that separates the model, parameters, frozen configuration, data,
estimator, audit family, result, provenance, and status,
Equation (119.1) is DETERMINISTIC_TYPE_NORMALIZATION. It is the chapter's audit contract, not a recovered native
definition of any one assigned handle.
119.2 Parameter vector
The quantities allowed to vary in an analysis can be collected as
Equation (119.2) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. The parameter space must specify dimensions, allowed
domains, priors or constraints, and conventions before estimation is meaningful.
119.3 Frozen configuration
A parameter freeze binds values, code, equations, preprocessing, and decision rules to a versioned content digest,
Equation (119.3) is DETERMINISTIC_AUDIT_NORMALIZATION. The hash records identity and immutability of the selected
configuration; it does not establish scientific correctness.
119.4 Likelihood-based estimation
For specified data and a probabilistic forward model, a maximum-likelihood estimate has the scaffold
Equation (119.4) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. It requires an explicit likelihood, nuisance treatment,
identifiability analysis, and recorded optimization procedure.
119.5 Posterior estimation
Bayesian updating is represented by
Equation (119.5) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Prior, likelihood, evidence approximation, sampling
diagnostics, and posterior summaries belong in the frozen analysis record.
119.6 Dimensionality audit
Every equality intended as a physical equation must satisfy the necessary condition
Equation (119.6) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Dimensional agreement can reject malformed expressions,
but it neither proves a derivation nor selects a unique physical law.

130.1 Typed formulation record
A historical formulation must distinguish identity, exact content, source, chronology, object vocabulary, equations, relations,
declared status, supersession evidence, and uncertainty,
Equation (130.1) is DETERMINISTIC_TYPE_NORMALIZATION. It prevents a historical title from being mistaken for a fully

Equation (130.2) is DETERMINISTIC_AUDIT_NORMALIZATION. Occurrence provenance remains distinct even when exact

130.3 Formulation difference

Equation (130.3) is DETERMINISTIC_AUDIT_NORMALIZATION. Text, objects, equations, relations, and status are compared
independently.
130.4 Source precedence

Equation (130.4) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Temporal precedence does not by itself imply logical or
canonical replacement.

Equation (130.5) is DETERMINISTIC_STATUS_NORMALIZATION. Each assignment requires exact source or curator
provenance.

Equation (130.6) is DETERMINISTIC_AUDIT_NORMALIZATION. The predicate is not inferred from numbering or style.

Chapter 131 - Narrative Models and Scientific Translation
131.1 Typed narrative record
A narrative unit must distinguish exact text, source, speaker, scene role, imagery, proposed scientific referent, translation rule,
confidence, provenance, and status,
Equation (131.1) is DETERMINISTIC_TYPE_NORMALIZATION. It preserves narrative content without representing imagery
as an exact mathematical statement.
131.2 Candidate translation map
A curator may propose a typed translation
where a narrative unit maps to a set of candidate scientific objects. Equation (131.2) is CURATOR_SYNTHESIS. The map is
reviewable and is not source-supplied unless explicit evidence says otherwise.
131.3 Many-to-one translation
Different images may express the same candidate structure,
Equation (131.3) is DETERMINISTIC_TYPE_NORMALIZATION. Repetition across scenes can support convergence but does
not multiply substantive evidence automatically.
131.4 One-to-many ambiguity
A single image may admit several candidate readings,
Equation (131.4) is DETERMINISTIC_STATUS_NORMALIZATION. Ambiguity is retained instead of silently choosing the most
convenient referent.
131.5 Structural invariant set
A translation may preserve only declared structural features,
Equation (131.5) is CURATOR_SYNTHESIS. Each retained feature requires exact textual and object-level support.
131.6 Translation loss
The information not carried into a scientific model remains explicit,
Equation (131.6) is DETERMINISTIC_AUDIT_NORMALIZATION. Voice, emotion, setting, and narrative purpose are not
erased by translation.

132.1 Typed ruling record

Equation (132.2) is DETERMINISTIC_AUDIT_NORMALIZATION. A ruling may organize unresolved evidence, but authority

Equation (132.6) is DETERMINISTIC_TYPE_NORMALIZATION. Scope cannot be expanded by analogy or convenience.

Chapter 133 - Philosophical Interpretation
133.1 Typed interpretation record
A philosophical interpretation must distinguish exact source, target object, thesis, premises, inferential rule, alternatives,
counterarguments, evidence, scope, and status,
Equation (133.1) is DETERMINISTIC_TYPE_NORMALIZATION. It separates interpretation from source statement,
mathematical proof, and empirical result.
133.2 Argument form
An interpretive conclusion requires declared premises and inference,
Equation (133.2) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. A title, image, or formal resemblance cannot substitute for
the missing premises.
133.3 Underdetermination
One evidence set may admit several interpretations,
Equation (133.3) is DETERMINISTIC_STATUS_NORMALIZATION. Competing readings remain visible until additional
evidence discriminates them.
133.4 Philosophical coordinates
Interpretive claims can be separated by question type,
Equation (133.4) is DETERMINISTIC_TYPE_NORMALIZATION. Answers in one coordinate do not automatically settle the
others.
133.5 Stance vocabulary
A controlled stance set is
Equation (133.5) is DETERMINISTIC_STATUS_NORMALIZATION. The labels organize readings rather than decide which is
true.
133.6 Emergence and reduction
An emergence claim and a reduction claim are distinct,
Equation (133.6) is DETERMINISTIC_TYPE_NORMALIZATION. Each direction requires its own map, scale, conditions, and
explanatory standard.

Chapter 134 - Public Disclosure and Research-Library Boundary
134.1 Typed disclosure record
A disclosure decision must distinguish the retained research record, the proposed release object, audience, permissions,
exclusions, provenance, validation, and status,
Equation (134.1) is DETERMINISTIC_TYPE_NORMALIZATION. It prevents the existence of a recovered record from being
mistaken for authorization to publish it.
134.2 Research and publication states
The internal research state and a public state are separately typed,
Equation (134.2) is DETERMINISTIC_STATUS_NORMALIZATION. A curated research library may contain candidates,
historical variants, conflicts, and unresolved requirements that a public release must label explicitly.
134.3 Promotion is an operation
Public disclosure requires a governed transformation rather than an implicit copy,
Equation (134.3) is CURATOR_SYNTHESIS. No assigned source defines this operator, so its domain, authorization, and
implementation remain publication-policy work.
134.4 Admission predicate
A candidate public object can be represented by a conjunctive admission test,
Equation (134.4) is DETERMINISTIC_TYPE_NORMALIZATION. Here quality, status, provenance, consent or clearance, and
audience suitability are independent checks; the formula does not assert that any present record has passed them.
134.5 Status preservation
Release formatting must not promote evidentiary status,
unless a separately recorded ruling changes that status. Equation (134.5) is DETERMINISTIC_STATUS_NORMALIZATION.
Publication is not proof, canonization, or empirical confirmation.
134.6 Provenance closure
Every released claim requires a traceable source path,
Equation (134.6) is CURATOR_SYNTHESIS. The required path includes exact evidence, transformations, review decisions,
and release metadata.

Chapter 135 - Symbol and Type Dictionary
135.1 Dictionary entry
A mathematical dictionary entry must separate the API identity, displayed symbol, type, domain, codomain, scope, status, and
provenance,
Equation (135.1) is DETERMINISTIC_TYPE_NORMALIZATION. A familiar glyph is not a complete definition because its
namespace, scope, and type determine how it may be used.
135.2 Handle identity
Canonical identity is controlled by the handle and URI pair,
Equation (135.2) is DETERMINISTIC_API_NORMALIZATION. Titles and local symbols may vary, while the exact address pair
prevents distinct records from being merged accidentally.
135.3 Symbol assignment
A symbol assignment is a scoped map,
Equation (135.3) is DETERMINISTIC_TYPE_NORMALIZATION. The same glyph may be reused in another source or formal
system only if its scope remains explicit.
135.4 Typed maps
Every operator or construction requires a signature,
Equation (135.4) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Without domain and codomain, composition, equality,
inversion, and dimensional checks remain underdetermined.
135.5 Composition rule
Two maps compose only when their intermediate types agree,
Equation (135.5) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. A graph path does not supply this mathematical
compatibility by itself.
135.6 Equality boundary
Symbol equality requires compatible type and scope,
Equation (135.6) is DETERMINISTIC_TYPE_NORMALIZATION. Matching labels or suffixes are insufficient evidence of
identity.

Chapter 136 - Equation Catalog
136.1 Catalog record
An equation catalog entry must retain the immutable record identifier, exact expression, environment, source unit, attached
handle, evidence class, and status,
Equation (136.1) is DETERMINISTIC_TYPE_NORMALIZATION. Cataloging an expression does not assert that it is an axiom,
theorem, derived result, or validated physical law.
136.2 Exact-expression identity
The identity of an exact expression is controlled by its stored text and provenance,
Equation (136.2) is DETERMINISTIC_PROVENANCE_NORMALIZATION. A normalized display form cannot silently replace
the source expression.
136.3 Attachment relation
One equation may be attached to several mathematical addresses,
Equation (136.3) is DETERMINISTIC_TYPE_NORMALIZATION. Multiple handle links are navigation records, not independent
equation occurrences.
136.4 Unique-count policy
Substantive equation counts use unique equation identifiers,
Equation (136.4) is DETERMINISTIC_COUNTING_NORMALIZATION. Duplicate attachments preserve provenance while
contributing one mathematical expression to the catalog.
136.5 Variant boundary
Textual similarity is not exact identity,
Equation (136.5) is EVIDENCE_BOUNDARY. Sign conventions, indices, factors, limits, and operator ordering may encode
material differences.
136.6 Mathematical equivalence boundary
Exact textual difference also does not prove inequivalence,
Equation (136.6) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Equivalence requires declared assumptions and a
derivation, not catalog-level normalization.

136.7 Equation signature
A typed equation requires both sides to inhabit a compatible space,
Equation (136.7) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Missing symbol types, domains, codomains, units, or index
conventions remain explicit catalog gaps.
136.8 Dimensional check
Where physical dimensions are declared, equality requires dimensional agreement,
Equation (136.8) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Passing this check is necessary but not sufficient for
physical validity.
136.9 Derivation record
A derivation is separately typed from its conclusion,
Equation (136.9) is DETERMINISTIC_TYPE_NORMALIZATION. Hypotheses and inference steps must be present before an
equation is represented as proved.
136.10 Status coordinates
An equation's status is a tuple rather than a single prestige label,
Equation (136.10) is DETERMINISTIC_STATUS_NORMALIZATION. Exact recovery, type completeness, proof, and empirical
confirmation are independent questions.
136.11 Graph boundary
An API dependency does not establish an algebraic derivation,
Equation (136.11) is EVIDENCE_BOUNDARY. Graph edges organize the address space and retain their own audit and
provenance fields.
136.12 Aggregate native profile
The twenty-six assigned addresses supply
Equation (136.12) is DETERMINISTIC_COVERAGE_EVIDENCE. Evidence is highly concentrated rather than uniformly
distributed across the assigned addresses.

Chapter 137 - Axioms and Primitives
137.1 Formal-system record
A formal-system entry must distinguish namespace, identifier, statement, symbol signature, scope, status, and provenance,
Equation (137.1) is DETERMINISTIC_TYPE_NORMALIZATION. A label such as A3 or P1 is not globally meaningful without its
namespace and exact source.
137.2 Axiom role
Within a declared formal system, an axiom is an admitted premise,
Equation (137.2) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Admission inside a framework does not establish empirical
truth or acceptance outside that framework.
137.3 Primitive role
A primitive is introduced without reduction to prior terms in the same presentation,
Equation (137.3) is DETERMINISTIC_TYPE_NORMALIZATION. It records a formal role, not metaphysical fundamentality.
137.4 Definition role
A definition introduces a term through an explicit defining relation,
Equation (137.4) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Definitions, axioms, primitives, lemmas, and theorems
therefore remain different record classes.
137.5 Derivation closure
The deductive closure of axioms under rules is
Equation (137.5) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. A catalog cannot assert membership in this closure when
hypotheses or inference steps are absent.
137.6 Independence boundary
An independence claim requires two non-derivability obligations,
Equation (137.6) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. No such proof is inferred from address labels or coverage
counts.
137.7 Consistency boundary
Syntactic consistency is the absence of a formula and its negation in the same closure,
A = (N, i, S, τ, Ω, σ, p).

Chapter 138 - Definitions
138.1 Definition record
A definition entry must preserve the canonical address, term, exact defining text, formal signature, scope, status, and
provenance,
Equation (138.1) is DETERMINISTIC_TYPE_NORMALIZATION. A declared title may identify a definition-shaped address while
the exact defining text remains absent from the coherent evidence layer.
138.2 Definitional equality
Definitional introduction is represented separately from proved equality,
Equation (138.2) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. The notation records a stipulated meaning within a scope; it
does not assert empirical identity.
138.3 Scope rule
A definition binds only inside its declared scope,
Equation (138.3) is DETERMINISTIC_TYPE_NORMALIZATION. Historical versions, namespaces, and source-local
conventions therefore remain distinct.
138.4 Conservative extension
A conservative definition should not add new consequences in the old vocabulary,
Equation (138.4) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Whether a recovered MK-43 definition is conservative
requires a specified theory and proof.
138.5 Well-formedness
A typed definition requires its definiens to inhabit the declared type,
Equation (138.5) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Missing domains, codomains, units, or index conventions
prevent a fully typed reconstruction.
138.6 Circularity boundary
A direct circular definition does not determine independent content,
Equation (138.6) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Fixed-point existence and uniqueness require additional
hypotheses.

Equation (138.7) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Lexical similarity does not supply the required derivation.

Equation (138.8) is DETERMINISTIC_TYPE_NORMALIZATION. This chapter therefore does not reclassify axiom-titled

138.9 Definition-versus-primitive boundary
A defined term and a primitive term are likewise distinct,
Equation (138.9) is DETERMINISTIC_TYPE_NORMALIZATION. Later versions may reorganize a theory, but such changes

Chapter 139 - Lemmas and Propositions
139.1 Result record
A lemma or proposition record must preserve its address, statement, hypotheses, conclusion, proof object, scope, status, and
provenance,
Equation (139.1) is DETERMINISTIC_TYPE_NORMALIZATION. A named result is not complete unless its exact statement and
proof obligations are recoverable.
139.2 Lemma role
A lemma is a proved intermediate result within a declared argument,
Equation (139.2) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. The label records intended formal role; proof status must
still be established independently.
139.3 Proposition role
A proposition is a typed assertion with stated hypotheses and conclusion,
Equation (139.3) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Neither terminology nor placement determines whether a
proof has been recovered.
139.4 Proof object
A proof object records ordered justified steps,
Equation (139.4) is DETERMINISTIC_TYPE_NORMALIZATION. Source citations and dependency edges do not substitute for
the inference rules $r_i$.
139.5 Hypothesis closure
A result may be applied only when all hypotheses have been discharged,
Equation (139.5) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Omitted hypotheses prevent a valid downstream
application.
139.6 Type preservation
Every inferential step must preserve well-formed types,
Equation (139.6) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. A visually plausible transition is not a typed derivation.

Chapter 140 - Theorems and Proof Status
140.1 Theorem record
A theorem record must preserve the canonical address, exact statement, hypotheses, conclusion, proof, formal system, status,
and provenance,
Equation (140.1) is DETERMINISTIC_TYPE_NORMALIZATION. A theorem title is an address-level claim about role, not
evidence that all proof fields are populated.
140.2 Proof judgment
A proved theorem requires an explicit derivation,
Equation (140.2) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. The formal system and inference rules must be identified for
the judgment to be auditable.
140.3 Soundness boundary
Semantic truth follows from syntactic proof only under soundness,
Equation (140.3) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Soundness itself requires justification.
140.4 Completeness boundary
Failure to recover a proof is not proof of falsehood,
Equation (140.4) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Missing evidence and refutation remain distinct statuses.
140.5 Proof-status coordinates
The status of a theorem-shaped record is multidimensional,
Equation (140.5) is DETERMINISTIC_STATUS_NORMALIZATION. Exact source recovery, mathematical proof, and empirical
validation do not collapse into one label.
140.6 Candidate boundary
A theorem candidate remains distinct from a proved theorem,
Equation (140.6) is EVIDENCE_BOUNDARY. Naming elegance or structural convergence cannot complete missing
mathematics.
140.7 Numerical boundary
Numerical agreement over a finite test set does not constitute a universal proof,
T = (h, S, H, C, π, F, σ, p).

Equation (142.1) is DETERMINISTIC_TYPE_NORMALIZATION. It is a comparison record, not an assertion that every MK-43

Equation (142.2) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. A source-specific state space cannot inherit Hilbert structure
merely from quantum terminology.

143.1 Graph convention record

provenance,
Equation (143.1) is DETERMINISTIC_TYPE_NORMALIZATION. It prevents a dependency graph, theorem graph, causal

Equation (143.3) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. A listed sequence of handles is not yet a mathematical

Equation (143.4) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. A dependency subgraph retains only the edge semantics
explicitly selected.

Equation (143.5) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Preservation of labels, weights, or edge types requires
additional conditions.

Equation (143.6) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Associativity and identity laws are required, not optional

Chapter 144 - API-Native Derivation Trees
144.1 Derivation-tree record
A derivation record must declare nodes, parent relation, root, premises, rule labels, conclusions, typing, status, and
provenance,
Equation (144.1) is DETERMINISTIC_TYPE_NORMALIZATION. An API neighborhood becomes a derivation tree only when its
edges carry valid inferential roles.
144.2 Rooted tree
A finite rooted tree has a distinguished root and a unique path from that root to every node,
Equation (144.2) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. A dependency graph with cycles or multiple ancestry paths
is not a tree without an explicit unfolding convention.
144.3 Parent map
For every nonroot node, a parent map may be written
Equation (144.3) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. The symbol is local to this appendix and is not a recovered
MK-43 projection operator.
144.4 Labeled inference node
If premises $P_1,\ldots,P_k$ support a conclusion $C$ under rule $R$, the node is displayed as
Equation (144.4) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. The rule must be named and its admissibility established in
the applicable formal system.
144.5 Derivation depth
The depth of a rooted derivation tree is
Equation (144.5) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Recursion depth and logical proof depth remain different
quantities unless a source types their relation.

Equation (144.7) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Such an order is not generally unique and does not by itself

144.8 Proof-obligation predicate
A candidate conclusion is closed only if all premise, rule, typing, and provenance obligations pass,
Equation (144.8) is CURATOR_SYNTHESIS. It is an audit predicate for the TOME, not a recovered framework axiom.

Equation (144.9) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Tree unfoldings may duplicate nodes but may not multiply

Chapter 145 - Dimensional and Normalization Ledger
145.1 Quantity convention record
A mathematical or physical quantity must preserve value, dimension, unit, normalization, scale, domain, status, and
provenance,
Equation (145.1) is DETERMINISTIC_TYPE_NORMALIZATION. Equal symbols from different sources cannot be identified
until these coordinates are compatible.
145.2 Dimension vector
Relative to declared base dimensions, write
Equation (145.2) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. The choice and ordering of base dimensions must be
stated.
145.3 Product rule
Dimensions multiply under products,
Equation (145.3) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Powers and quotients follow from the same exponent
arithmetic.
145.4 Additive compatibility
A sum is dimensionally admissible only when its terms share a dimension,
Equation (145.4) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Formal sums of differently typed objects require another
explicitly declared construction.
145.5 Derivative dimension
For a coordinate component,
Equation (145.5) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Coordinates cannot be treated as dimensionless without a
source convention.
145.6 Integration dimension
For an $n$-dimensional coordinate measure,
Equation (145.6) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Jacobians, density weights, and metric volume factors
remain explicit.

VOLUME XVIII - MATHEMATICAL APPENDICES
Chapter 146 - Provenance, Status, and Citation Ledgers
146.1 Provenance record
Every substantive claim must preserve record identity, claim class, source identity, exact locator, content hash, ancestry, status,
and recovery pass,
Equation (146.1) is DETERMINISTIC_TYPE_NORMALIZATION. Provenance is a typed chain, not a filename or an unqualified
citation count.
146.2 Content identity
Exact content identity is established by a cryptographic digest,
Equation (146.2) is EXTERNAL_ESTABLISHED_MATHEMATICS. Equal hashes support byte identity under the stated
algorithm; they do not establish semantic equivalence of different bytes.
146.3 Occurrence-to-content map
Physical occurrences map many-to-one onto unique content records,
Equation (146.3) is DETERMINISTIC_TYPE_NORMALIZATION. Every occurrence retains its path and ancestry while
duplicate content counts once substantively.
146.4 Citation record
A resolvable citation records source, locator, quoted or attached content hash, claim, and evidence class,
Equation (146.4) is DETERMINISTIC_TYPE_NORMALIZATION. A citation is incomplete when its immutable source location
cannot be reopened.
146.5 Status partial order
Evidence status must not be upgraded merely by repetition,
Equation (146.5) is DETERMINISTIC_STATUS_NORMALIZATION. Promotion requires the explicit review and proof conditions
attached to the target status.
146.6 Evidence-class separation
The principal evidence classes remain disjoint at the record level,
Equation (146.6) is CURATOR_SYNTHESIS. A record may have links across classes, but its own class cannot change silently.
P = (r, c, s, ℓ, h, a, σ, ρ).
